 Just another totally normal Tuesday (ft. SBA panic)
Hi Sara,
In my work as a deal attorney, I spend most of my week helping people buy, sell, and survive the realities of owning an accounting firm.
And on a typical Tuesday? 

I get at least one call from someone stressing about the debt they’re taking on with an SBA loan. 
Accountants are not reckless, they are measured people who want to know the contours of the risk before they take it on. 
But who can you ask? You can’t exactly ask the bank-they’re the ones you’re trying to convince to loan you money. You’re focused on convincing them you’re credit-worthy and nothing is particularly reassuring about asking what happens if you default. 
So here’s the answer to the question you can’t ask. BecauseI’m here to say the quiet part out loud for you. 
What happens if you can’t repay your SBA loan? 
Drum roll: exciting answer is: It depends. 
If you’re worried you might miss a payment, don’t wait until it happens.
Most lenders can help if they’re looped in early. That might look like adjusting your amortization schedule, pushing your first principal payments, or just giving you room to recalibrate.
But once the deadline passes without a word? The bank shifts into risk mode. And if it’s still early in your loan term, that can kick off some very unfun oversight and is very aggressive. 
This isn’t about being scared of your lender. It’s about giving yourself room to solve problems while you still have leverage.
If you're staring down a gap between what's due and what's doable, say something. Quiet doesn’t buy you time; it just shrinks your options.
What was the biggest financial surprise in your first year of ownership?
I’m always curious where the cracks show up first.
Less panic. More plan,
Sara Sharp
Deal Attorney & Founder, Deal Academy
